q: A 'counterfort retaining wall' is a retaining wall in which:

options.A: Triangular ribs, called counterforts, are provided on the earth side of the wall at intervals, connecting the wall face with its base slab and strengthening the wall against overturning
options.B: The wall is built of dry stones without any mortar throughout its height
options.C: Weep holes are omitted so that water is retained behind the wall
options.D: The wall rests on a group of piles driven in front of its toe

e: A counterfort retaining wall has triangular ribs on the earth side at intervals connecting the wall face to the base slab, strengthening it against overturning.

q: Tools and plant in the charge of a division which have become unserviceable are dealt with by:

options.A: Continuing to be shown in the tools and plant account indefinitely at their original value
options.B: Being handed over to the contractor executing the current work in lieu of his hire charges
options.C: Being surveyed by the competent officer or committee and, with the sanction of the competent authority, surveyed off, that is removed from the tools and plant account, and disposed of as provided in the rules
options.D: Being transferred to the Material-at-Site account of a work under execution

e: Unserviceable tools and plant are surveyed by the competent officer or committee and, with competent sanction, surveyed off the tools and plant account and disposed of as per rules.

q: The 'gable' of a building provided with a pitched roof is:

options.A: The sloping edge of the roof where it meets another sloping roof internally
options.B: The triangular portion of the end wall of the building, comprised between the sloping sides of the pitched roof
options.C: The lower edge of the sloping roof which projects beyond the face of the wall
options.D: The horizontal line at the top where the two slopes of the roof meet

e: The gable is the triangular portion of the end wall of a pitched-roof building enclosed between the two sloping sides of the roof.

q: Where the execution of a bridge work affects traffic on a public road crossing the site, the work is carried out:

options.A: After closing the road permanently to all traffic at the discretion of the contractor
options.B: Under a traffic diversion arrangement agreed in co-ordination with the road and police authorities, so that the road traffic is diverted safely while the work proceeds
options.C: Only during the night, road work in the day being prohibited in all cases
options.D: At the risk of the road users, no diversion arrangement being necessary

e: Bridge work affecting a public road is executed under a traffic diversion agreed with the road and police authorities, so road traffic passes safely while work proceeds.

q: 'Falsework' erected in connection with the construction of a bridge or a similar structure means:

options.A: The platform erected for the workmen to stand upon while working at a height
options.B: The temporary support given to an unsafe existing structure to prevent its collapse
options.C: The formwork provided for the vertical faces of concrete members
options.D: The temporary structure erected to support the formwork and the structure itself, such as a girder or a deck under casting, until the structure becomes capable of supporting itself

e: Falsework is the temporary structure supporting the formwork and the structure itself, such as a girder or deck under casting, until it can support itself.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An asset transferred from one Railway to another Railway is taken over by the receiving Railway at its recorded (book) value, the capital-at-charge of the two Railways being adjusted accordingly by transfer entries.
2. Such a transfer is settled by a cash payment of the market value of the asset by the receiving Railway to the transferring Railway in every case.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: inter-Railway asset transfers are taken over at book value with capital-at-charge adjusted by transfer entries. Statement 2 is wrong: no cash payment of market value is made.

q: The 'valley' of a pitched roof is:

options.A: The topmost horizontal line where the two main slopes of the roof meet
options.B: The sloping edge at the end of the roof over the gable wall
options.C: The internal angle or groove formed where two sloping surfaces of the roof meet, which collects and leads away the rain water from both the surfaces
options.D: The sheet fixed over the ridge of the roof to make it watertight

e: The valley is the internal angle or groove where two sloping roof surfaces meet; it collects rain water from both surfaces and leads it away.

q: A sub-contractor engaged by a works contractor for a portion of the work has a grievance about the payment due to him for that portion. His claim for that payment lies:

options.A: Directly against the Railways, with whom he is treated as being in contract
options.B: Against the main contractor alone, there being no direct contractual relationship between the sub-contractor and the Railways
options.C: Against the Tender Committee which recommended the main contract
options.D: Against the Engineer personally, who approved the sub-contracting

e: There is no privity of contract between a sub-contractor and the Railways, so his payment claim lies only against the main contractor who engaged him.

q: 'Prestressed concrete' used in structures such as bridge girders is concrete in which:

options.A: High-tensile steel tendons are stretched and anchored so as to introduce a pre-compression in the concrete, which counteracts the tensile stresses coming on the member under load
options.B: A richer proportion of cement is used than in ordinary reinforced concrete
options.C: The reinforcement is placed in the concrete without any stress in it, as in ordinary reinforced concrete
options.D: Steel fibres are mixed in the concrete to increase its tensile strength

e: In prestressed concrete, high-tensile tendons are stretched and anchored to induce pre-compression, counteracting tensile stresses under load in members like bridge girders.

q: A works contractor has demanded arbitration in accordance with the contract, but the Railways fail to appoint the arbitrator within the period provided for the purpose. In such a case, the contractor may:

options.A: Appoint an arbitrator of his own choice whose award will bind the Railways
options.B: Treat the contract as determined and stop all further proceedings
options.C: Recover his claim directly from the security deposit of the work
options.D: Apply to the court under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 for the appointment of the arbitrator

e: If the Railways fail to appoint the arbitrator within the stipulated period, the contractor may apply to the court under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 for appointment.

q: The 'landing' provided in a staircase of a building is:

options.A: The sloping member which supports the steps of a flight
options.B: The vertical face of a step between two successive treads
options.C: A level platform provided between two flights of steps, or at the top of a flight, where a person can rest or change direction
options.D: The protective railing provided along the open side of the staircase

e: A landing is the level platform between two flights of steps, or at the top of a flight, provided for rest or change of direction in a staircase.

q: An agreement to do an act which is impossible in itself from the very beginning is:

options.A: Valid until the time fixed for its performance arrives
options.B: Void from the outset, the impossibility existing at the time the agreement is made itself making it void
options.C: Enforceable if the party promising it pays compensation in advance
options.D: Treated as a contract which has become impossible only after it is made

e: Under Section 56 of the Contract Act principle, an agreement to do an act impossible from the very beginning is void ab initio; it is not merely void when performance falls due.

q: A 'ranging rod' used in chain surveying for a proposed work is a rod which is used for:

options.A: Establishing a straight line between survey stations and locating intermediate points on the survey line, the rod being painted in alternate bands so that it is visible from a distance
options.B: Measuring the length of the survey line directly in the field
options.C: Determining the reduced level of the points along the survey line
options.D: Setting out a right angle at a point on the survey line

e: A ranging rod, painted in alternate visible bands, is used to establish a straight line between survey stations and locate intermediate points on the survey line.

q: An officer of the Railways has a personal or financial interest in a firm which has tendered for a work which the officer is dealing with. The correct course for the officer is to:

options.A: Deal with the tender himself, recording that his interest is only indirect
options.B: Decide the tender in favour of another firm without disclosing his interest
options.C: Continue to deal with the tender after informing the tenderers of his interest
options.D: Disclose his interest to his superior authority and abstain from dealing with that tender

e: An officer with a personal or financial interest in a tendering firm must disclose the interest to his superior and abstain from dealing with that tender, avoiding conflict of interest.

q: A 'total station' used in the survey of a proposed railway work is an instrument which:

options.A: Measures only the horizontal distances between points along the alignment
options.B: Combines the measurement of horizontal and vertical angles with electronic measurement of distances, so that the positions and levels of points are obtained and recorded electronically
options.C: Records the levels of points with reference to a datum, like a dumpy level
options.D: Measures the cross-section of the formation at a chainage directly

e: A total station combines angular measurement with electronic distance measurement, giving positions and levels of points electronically in one instrument.

q: Before proceedings for the acquisition of land for a railway project are completed, the land proposed to be acquired is jointly measured by the representatives of the Railways and of the revenue authorities primarily in order to:

options.A: Fix the rates at which the construction work on the land will be tendered
options.B: Decide the alignment of the line finally for the detailed estimate
options.C: Ascertain on the ground the area and the particulars of the land to be acquired, on the basis of which the acquisition proceedings and the award of compensation proceed
options.D: Hand over the land to the contractor who will construct the project

e: Joint measurement by Railway and revenue representatives ascertains on the ground the area and particulars of land to be acquired, forming the basis of acquisition proceedings and compensation award.

q: An 'aqueduct', as a cross-drainage work, is a structure in which:

options.A: A canal or channel is carried over a natural drainage or depression, the drainage passing below the channel
options.B: A drainage is carried over a canal in a trough supported on piers
options.C: A drainage is passed under a canal under pressure, through a barrel working full
options.D: A road is carried over a railway line on a bridge

e: In an aqueduct, a canal or channel is carried over a natural drainage or depression, with the drainage passing below the channel.

q: In making the allotment of funds for works for a year, the claims ordinarily provided for in preference to altogether new starts are those of:

options.A: Works proposed for inclusion in the Works Programme of the following year
options.B: Deposit works expected to be received from outside bodies during the year
options.C: Works of other Railways which may be transferred during the year
options.D: Works already in progress and the liabilities already committed on sanctioned works, so that such works are not held up or left incomplete for want of funds

e: In fund allotment, works in progress and committed liabilities on sanctioned works get preference over new starts, so ongoing works are not held up or left incomplete for want of funds.

q: A 'geotextile' laid in connection with the formation of a track or an embankment is:

options.A: A sheet of impervious plastic laid over the roof of a building for waterproofing
options.B: A permeable synthetic fabric laid between the layers of the formation, which separates the layers, and allows drainage and filtration, so that the ballast and the formation soil do not get mixed up
options.C: A fabric net spread over the slopes of a cutting to hold the turfing in place
options.D: The cloth used for curing the concrete laid in a work

e: A geotextile is a permeable synthetic fabric laid between formation layers for separation, drainage and filtration, preventing mixing of ballast and formation soil.

q: Before a newly constructed line is sanctioned to be opened for passenger traffic, the inspection of the line by the Commissioner of Railway Safety ordinarily includes:

options.A: A check of the contractor's final bill by the Commissioner personally
options.B: The sanction of the completion report of the project by the Commissioner
options.C: A trial run over the line, in addition to the inspection of the works, so that the running of trains over the line is tested before it is opened
options.D: The approval of the rates accepted for the works of the line

e: CRS inspection before opening a new line includes, besides inspection of works, a trial run over the line to test actual train running before passenger opening.

q: The 'compaction factor' used as a measure of the workability of concrete is:

options.A: The ratio of the weight of concrete which is partially compacted by the standard method to the weight of the same concrete when fully compacted
options.B: The depth to which a standard cone sinks in the fresh concrete under its own weight
options.C: The ratio of the water content of the mix to its cement content
options.D: The time taken by the concrete to flow out of a standard apparatus completely

e: The compaction factor is the ratio of the weight of concrete partially compacted by the standard method to the weight of the same concrete when fully compacted; it measures workability.

q: Under a services contract for the upkeep of a station, a number of the staff deployed by the contractor are absent on a day. In regard to the service for that day, the contractor is required to:

options.A: Suspend the service for the day, the Railways having no remedy in the matter
options.B: Pay the wages of the absent staff to the Railways in cash
options.C: Obtain an extension of the currency of the contract for the period of absence
options.D: Provide substitute hands in place of the absent staff, so that the service contracted for is rendered without interruption

e: Under a services contract, the contractor must provide substitute hands for absent staff so the contracted service continues without interruption; absence does not suspend the service.

q: A 'plate load test' carried out at the site of a foundation is a field test in which:

options.A: A sample of the soil is taken to the laboratory in a core cutter for density determination
options.B: A rigid plate placed at the foundation level is loaded in stages and its settlement is observed, so that the bearing capacity and settlement behaviour of the soil are assessed
options.C: A standard rod is driven into the soil by blows of a standard hammer and the resistance is counted
options.D: The soil below the foundation is explored by boring and the strata are recorded

e: In a plate load test, a rigid plate at foundation level is loaded in stages and settlement observed, assessing the soil's bearing capacity and settlement behaviour.

q: Consignments of materials such as steel and cement brought to a work by a contractor are accepted for use on the work after:

options.A: The contractor produces a declaration that the materials are of the required quality
options.B: The materials are weighed at the site, weight alone being the test of quality
options.C: The manufacturer's test certificates accompanying the consignments are checked and the prescribed tests are carried out, so that the materials are found to conform to the specifications
options.D: The Tender Committee certifies the quality of each consignment

e: Contractor-supplied materials like steel and cement are accepted only after the manufacturer's test certificates are checked and prescribed tests confirm conformity with specifications.

q: The 'plasticity index' of a soil is:

options.A: The difference between the liquid limit and the plastic limit of the soil, indicating the range of moisture content over which the soil behaves as a plastic material
options.B: The ratio of the weight of water in the soil to the weight of the soil solids
options.C: The moisture content at which the soil passes from the liquid state to the plastic state
options.D: The percentage of clay particles present in the soil by weight

e: Plasticity index = liquid limit minus plastic limit of the soil, indicating the moisture range over which the soil behaves plastically.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An Integrity Pact executed for a major tender commits both the Railways and the bidders to avoid corrupt practices in the tender process.
2. Complaints arising under such an Integrity Pact are examined by the Independent External Monitors appointed for the purpose.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: an Integrity Pact binds the Railways and bidders against corrupt practices, and complaints under it are examined by the Independent External Monitors.

q: In a turnout, a 'facing point' is a switch which:

options.A: A train approaches from the crossing side, passing over the crossing before it reaches the switch rails
options.B: A train approaches at the toe of the switch, meeting the movable switch rails first, before passing over the crossing
options.C: Is provided only at the exit of a siding for trapping runaway vehicles
options.D: Is operated from the cabin by a lever frame in every case

e: At a facing point, a train approaches at the toe of the switch and meets the movable switch rails first, before passing over the crossing.

q: 'Post-qualification' of tenderers, as followed in ordinary works tenders where no separate pre-qualification is prescribed, means that:

options.A: The credentials of the tenderers are examined only after the work has been completed
options.B: The tenderers are shortlisted before the tenders are invited, and bids are called only from the shortlisted firms
options.C: The successful tenderer is enlisted for future works on the basis of his performance on the work
options.D: The eligibility and credentials of the tenderers are assessed after the bids are opened, from the documents submitted by them along with their bids, instead of through a separate shortlisting stage held before the bidding

e: In post-qualification, eligibility and credentials are assessed after bids are opened, from documents submitted with the bids, instead of a separate pre-bidding shortlisting stage.

q: The Railways make a demand under a bank guarantee furnished by a works contractor. The contractor disputes the Railways' claim and asks the bank to withhold payment until the dispute is decided. The correct position for the bank is that it:

options.A: Must withhold payment until the dispute between the Railways and the contractor is finally settled
options.B: Must decide the dispute itself and pay only if it finds the Railways' claim justified
options.C: May pay only with the written consent of the contractor who furnished the guarantee
options.D: Must pay on a proper demand made in accordance with the guarantee, without going into the merits of the underlying dispute between the Railways and the contractor

e: A bank guarantee is independent of the underlying dispute; on a proper demand conforming to the guarantee, the bank must pay without going into the merits of the dispute.

q: 'Coursed rubble masonry' used in the construction of walls and foundations consists of:

options.A: Roughly dressed stones laid in regular courses with mortar, the stones in each course being of about the same height and the vertical joints being broken between successive courses
options.B: Stones of irregular shapes and sizes laid without any mortar and without any courses
options.C: Finely dressed stones with very thin joints, used only for the face work of important structures
options.D: Bricks laid in courses with cement mortar in the foundation of a building

e: Coursed rubble masonry uses roughly dressed stones of about equal height laid in regular courses with mortar, with vertical joints broken between successive courses.

q: A formal agreement executed between a Zonal Railway and a contractor for a works contract is, in accordance with Article 299 of the Constitution, expressed to be made in the name of:

options.A: The General Manager of the Railway
options.B: The President of India
options.C: The Railway Board
options.D: The Principal Chief Engineer of the Railway

e: Under Article 299 of the Constitution, contracts on behalf of the Government of India are expressed to be made in the name of the President of India.

q: A contractor, which is a company, is paid an on-account bill of Rs 12,00,000 for a works contract. Tax deducted at source under Section 194C of the Income-tax Act, at 2 per cent, amounts to:
e: TDS under Section 194C at 2 per cent for a company payee = 2 per cent of Rs 12,00,000 = Rs 24,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before a new electrical (traction) installation on the Railways is energised and brought into regular use, the sanction of the Electrical Inspector to the Government of India (EIG) is required.
2. A newly constructed railway line is opened for the public carriage of passengers on the sanction of the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO).
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: EIG sanction is required before a new traction electrical installation is energised. Statement 2 is wrong: a new line opens on CRS sanction, not RDSO sanction.

q: A 'brick bat' used in brickwork is:

options.A: A brick which has been under-burnt in the kiln and is rejected for use in the work
options.B: A brick laid with its longest face exposed on the face of the wall
options.C: The depression formed on one face of a hand-moulded brick
options.D: A portion of a brick, commonly a half or a three-quarter piece, cut for use in closing the bond or in making up the required length in a course

e: A brick bat is a portion of a brick, commonly half or three-quarter, cut for closing the bond or making up the required length in a course.

q: A person whose relationship with a party to a contractual dispute falls within the Seventh Schedule of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996:

options.A: Is preferred for appointment as arbitrator in that dispute because of his familiarity with the party
options.B: Is ineligible to be appointed as an arbitrator in that dispute
options.C: Can be appointed as arbitrator if the other party raises no objection within seven days
options.D: Can act as the conciliator in that dispute without any restriction

e: A person whose relationship with a party falls in the Seventh Schedule of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is ineligible for appointment as arbitrator in that dispute.

q: The 'hip' of a pitched roof is:

options.A: The internal groove formed where two sloping surfaces of the roof meet
options.B: The horizontal line at the very top where the two main slopes of the roof meet
options.C: The inclined external angle formed where two sloping surfaces of the roof meet at the end of the roof, running from the ridge down to the eaves
options.D: The triangular portion of the end wall comprised between the sloping sides of the roof

e: The hip is the inclined external angle where two sloping roof surfaces meet at the end of the roof, running from the ridge down to the eaves.

q: Before the bills of a contractor for a work or a service are passed for payment, he is ordinarily required to produce proof of:

options.A: His income-tax assessment for the previous year
options.B: His registration under the Companies Act
options.C: Insurance of his own office premises and godowns
options.D: Payment of wages to his workmen and deposit of the Employees' Provident Fund and Employees' State Insurance contributions in respect of them

e: Before bills are passed, the contractor must prove payment of wages to his workmen and deposit of EPF and ESI contributions for them, as required under GCC and labour law conditions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The standard designs and drawings for bridges and other structures, to be adopted by the Zonal Railways, are prepared separately by the standards cell of each Zonal Railway for its own use.
2. A new material or product proposed for use in the permanent way can be adopted only after the approval of the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO), after trials where required.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong: standard designs are issued centrally, not prepared separately by each zonal standards cell. Statement 2 is correct: new permanent way materials need RDSO approval after trials where required.

q: 'Flashing' provided in the roof and walls of a building consists of:

options.A: A coat of waterproofing compound painted over the whole surface of the roof slab
options.B: Strips of impervious material, such as metal sheet, fixed at the junctions of the roof with walls, parapets and chimneys so as to prevent rain water from entering the joints
options.C: A layer of tiles laid over the roof slab to give a finished appearance to the roof
options.D: The groove cut under a coping or a sill to throw off rain water from the face of the wall

e: Flashing consists of strips of impervious material like metal sheet fixed at junctions of roof with walls, parapets and chimneys to stop rain water entering the joints.

q: A works contract is determined on account of the contractor's default, and disputes arising out of the contract remain unsettled. In this position, the arbitration clause contained in the contract:

options.A: Comes to an end automatically along with the determination of the contract
options.B: Can be invoked only in respect of work executed after the determination
options.C: Continues to operate for the settlement of the disputes arising out of the contract, even after the contract has been terminated
options.D: Is replaced by the decision of the Engineer on all the disputes

e: The arbitration clause is separable from the main contract, so it survives termination of the contract and can be invoked for disputes arising out of it.

q: Under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, the registration of an establishment which engages contract labour on a railway work is required to be obtained by:

options.A: The contractor who supplies the labour
options.B: The licensing officer appointed under the Act
options.C: The recognised trade union of the establishment
options.D: The principal employer, that is, the Railways

e: Under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, registration of the establishment is obtained by the principal employer, i.e. the Railways, not the contractor.

q: A 'stepped footing' is provided in the foundation of a wall or a column when:

options.A: The ground at the site is sloping, or the level at which the firm bearing stratum is available varies, so that the base of the footing is formed in steps to rest at the proper depth without excessive excavation or depth of foundation at any point
options.B: The footing is spread under the whole area of the building as a single slab
options.C: Two isolated footings are connected by a beam for distributing the loads of the columns
options.D: The foundation is carried deep below the scour level of a stream

e: A stepped footing is used on sloping ground or where the firm stratum level varies, the base being formed in steps to reach proper depth without excessive excavation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the case of a newly constructed railway line, the liability to pay dividend on its capital-at-charge is deferred, and kept as a deferred dividend liability, during the period of construction and the first five years after the line is opened to traffic.
2. The rate of dividend payable by the Railways to the general revenues on their capital-at-charge is determined on the basis of the recommendations of the Railway Convention Committee, as adopted by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: dividend on a new line's capital is deferred during construction and the first five years after opening as deferred dividend liability, and the dividend rate follows Railway Convention Committee recommendations adopted by Parliament.

q: In a cost-plus contract for the execution of a work, the verification of the cost payable to the contractor is secured by the condition that:

options.A: The cost is certified by the contractor's own auditor alone and is not open to examination by the Railways
options.B: The contractor is required to maintain proper cost records of the work, which are open to inspection by the Railways, so that the actual cost claimed by him can be verified
options.C: The cost is taken as whatever amount the contractor claims in his final bill
options.D: The contractor's books of account are treated as confidential and cannot be called for by the Railways

e: In a cost-plus contract, the contractor must maintain proper cost records open to Railway inspection, so the actual cost claimed can be verified before payment.

q: An 'under-reamed pile' provided in the foundation of a structure is a pile which:

options.A: Derives its capacity mainly from the friction developed along its shaft over its full length
options.B: Is driven at an inclination to resist the horizontal thrust coming on the structure
options.C: Is cast in a bore hole and is withdrawn after the concrete has set
options.D: Has one or more enlarged bulbs formed near its base, and is adopted particularly in expansive soils such as black cotton soil, where the bulbs anchor the pile against the uplift caused by the swelling of the soil

e: An under-reamed pile has enlarged bulbs near its base and is used in expansive soils like black cotton soil, the bulbs anchoring it against uplift from soil swelling.

q: After the tenders for a work have been opened, a tenderer asks for permission to revise the rates quoted by him and to add a condition to his offer. The correct position is that the tenderer:

options.A: Cannot be permitted to change the substance of his tender after it has been opened
options.B: May revise his rates freely until the Letter of Acceptance is issued
options.C: May withdraw his tender at this stage without forfeiture of his earnest money
options.D: May impose fresh conditions on his offer with the approval of the tender-opening official

e: After tenders are opened, no tenderer can be allowed to change the substance of his tender, revise rates or add conditions; the offer stands as submitted.

q: The 'void ratio' of a soil is the ratio of:

options.A: The weight of water present in the soil to the weight of the soil solids
options.B: The volume of the soil solids to the total volume of the soil mass
options.C: The volume of the voids in the soil mass to the volume of the soil solids
options.D: The total volume of the soil mass to the volume of the voids in it

e: Void ratio is the ratio of the volume of voids in the soil mass to the volume of soil solids.

q: A division is framing the programme of annual (ordinary) repairs of its buildings for the year. Which of the following is properly included in that programme as an ordinary repair item?

options.A: Complete rebuilding of a structure which has outlived its life
options.B: Periodical services such as whitewashing, colour washing and painting, carried out at the prescribed intervals, together with petty repairs
options.C: Renewal of the entire roof structure of the building
options.D: Addition of new rooms and floors to the existing building

e: Ordinary (annual) repairs cover periodical services like whitewashing, colour washing and painting at prescribed intervals plus petty repairs; rebuilding, full roof renewal and additions are not ordinary repairs.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Social Service Obligations of the Railways represent the losses borne by the Railways on uneconomic services and facilities provided in the larger public interest, such as uneconomic branch lines and concessional fares.
2. In recognition of these obligations, the Government grants the Railways relief in the dividend payable on the capital invested in strategic lines and certain other specified lines.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Social Service Obligations are losses on uneconomic services run in public interest, and Government grants dividend relief on capital of strategic and specified lines in recognition of them.

q: The 'permeability' of a soil is the property by virtue of which:

options.A: The soil changes its volume with changes in its moisture content
options.B: The soil resists the penetration of a standard rod driven into it by blows
options.C: The soil can be compacted to its maximum density at the optimum moisture content
options.D: Water flows through the interconnected voids of the soil mass under a hydraulic gradient

e: Permeability is the property by which water flows through the interconnected voids of a soil mass under a hydraulic gradient.

q: Under the 'Bid Security Declaration' introduced in Government procurement in lieu of earnest money deposit, a bidder who signs the declaration accepts that:

options.A: He will be suspended from participating in the tender process for the period specified in the bid documents, if he withdraws or modifies his bid during its validity, or if, after the award of the work, he fails to execute the contract or to furnish the performance security
options.B: His security deposit under all his other contracts with the Railways will be forfeited if he withdraws his bid
options.C: He will pay a penalty equal to twice the earnest money if his tender is not accepted
options.D: His bid will be treated as the lowest bid for the work for all purposes

e: Under the Bid Security Declaration (GFR), a bidder who withdraws or modifies his bid in validity, or fails to execute the contract or furnish performance security after award, is suspended from the tender process for the period specified in the bid documents.

q: 'Creep' in connection with hardened concrete in a structure refers to:

options.A: The immediate elastic shortening of the member as soon as the load is applied on it
options.B: The slow and continuing deformation of the concrete under a sustained load, which goes on with time after the initial elastic deformation has taken place
options.C: The shrinkage of the concrete which takes place as it dries after curing
options.D: The flow of fresh concrete into the formwork at the time of its placing

e: Creep is the slow, time-dependent continuing deformation of hardened concrete under sustained load, beyond the initial elastic deformation.

q: A sanctioned work is abandoned after it has been partly executed, and it is decided not to proceed with it further. The net infructuous expenditure incurred on the work is dealt with by:

options.A: Carrying it forward indefinitely under a works suspense head
options.B: Recovering it from the contractor who executed the part work
options.C: Charging it to the cost of the next work sanctioned in the division
options.D: Writing it off with the sanction of the competent authority, after taking over or disposing of the useful materials and assets created by the part work

e: Infructuous expenditure on an abandoned sanctioned work is written off with the sanction of the competent authority, after taking over or disposing of useful materials and assets created.

q: 'Laitance' noticed in connection with concrete work is:

options.A: A weak and friable layer of fine material and cement slurry which rises to, and forms on, the top surface of freshly placed concrete, and which is removed before the next lift of concrete is placed over it
options.B: The white deposit which appears on the surface of masonry due to the salts present in the bricks
options.C: The honeycombed portion of concrete in which the mortar has failed to fill the voids between the coarse aggregate
options.D: The excess water which appears on the surface of fresh concrete after it has been compacted

e: Laitance is the weak, friable layer of fines and cement slurry forming on the top surface of freshly placed concrete; it is removed before the next lift is placed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the MSMED Act, payment due to a micro or small enterprise for the goods or services supplied by it is required to be made within the period agreed with it, which cannot exceed 45 days.
2. Where such payment is delayed beyond the period specified, interest is payable to the enterprise at twice the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: under the MSMED Act, payment to a micro or small enterprise must be made within the agreed period, not exceeding 45 days. Statement 2 is wrong: delayed interest is at three times the RBI-notified bank rate, not twice, so only statement 1 holds.

q: 'Lacing' provided in a built-up steel column consists of:

options.A: The plates welded over the joints of the column at its ends for connecting it to the beam
options.B: The packing plates placed between the flanges of the column at the points of connection
options.C: Flat bars or angles connecting the two main components of the built-up column to one another, so that the components act together as a single unit against buckling
options.D: The bolts provided at the base of the column for anchoring it to its foundation

e: Lacing consists of flat bars or angles connecting the two main components of a built-up steel column so they act together as one unit against buckling.

q: Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways are made:

options.A: Mainly out of the borrowings raised by the Railways from the market
options.B: From revenue, keeping in view the renewals and replacements of assets which are falling due
options.C: Out of the proceeds of the sale of surplus railway land
options.D: By transfer from the Capital Fund of the Railways

e: Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund are made from revenue, keeping in view the renewals and replacements of assets falling due.

q: The 'slenderness ratio' of a steel column or strut is the ratio of:

options.A: The length of the member to its cross-sectional area
options.B: The load carried by the member to its cross-sectional area
options.C: The effective length of the member to its total length as fabricated
options.D: The effective length of the member to its least radius of gyration

e: Slenderness ratio = effective length of the column or strut divided by its least radius of gyration.

q: The cost of renewing or replacing an existing asset of the Railways is booked on:

options.A: Replacement Account
options.B: Additional Account
options.C: The Material-at-Site account of the work
options.D: The suspense account, pending the sanction of the completion report

e: Renewal or replacement of an existing railway asset is charged to the Replacement Account, the head under which replacement expenditure financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund is accounted.

q: The 'impact allowance' provided in the design of a railway bridge is an allowance made for:

options.A: The effect of the wind pressure acting on the train and the bridge together
options.B: The future increase expected in the axle loads of the rolling stock
options.C: The additional effect produced by the moving loads, over and above their static effect, on account of the dynamic action of the traffic passing over the bridge
options.D: The settlement expected in the foundations of the bridge after its construction

e: Impact allowance in bridge design covers the additional dynamic effect of moving loads over their static effect, caused by the action of traffic passing over the bridge.

q: In a track section, a small stock of rails, sleepers and fittings is kept with the sectional engineering staff itself, instead of every requirement being drawn from the stores depot. This stock, held as 'imprest stock', is meant:

options.A: For sale to the contractors executing works in the section
options.B: For use only on new construction works taken up in the section
options.C: For meeting urgent day-to-day maintenance requirements of the section, without waiting for a regular issue of the materials from the stores depot
options.D: As a reserve which can be opened only on the orders of the General Manager

e: Imprest stock of rails, sleepers and fittings is held with sectional staff to meet urgent day-to-day maintenance needs without waiting for regular stores issues.

q: In compass surveying for a proposed railway work, 'local attraction' means:

options.A: The angle between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian at a station
options.B: The attraction exerted by a long welded rail on the rails adjoining it in hot weather
options.C: The error introduced in the bearings by the careless centring of the compass over the station
options.D: The disturbance of the compass needle from the magnetic meridian by local magnetic influences, such as iron structures and masses of iron near the station, which falsifies the bearings observed there

e: Local attraction is the disturbance of the compass needle from the magnetic meridian by nearby magnetic influences like iron structures, which falsifies bearings in compass surveying.

q: The cost of construction of a work amounts to Rs 80,00,000. The cess leviable under the Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act, at 1 per cent of the cost of construction, recovered from the contractor's bills, amounts to:
e: BOCW welfare cess = 1 per cent of Rs 80,00,000 = Rs 80,000, recovered from the contractor's bills.

q: A 'cross staff' used in chain surveying for a proposed work is an instrument which is used for:

options.A: Setting out a right angle at a point on the survey line, so that perpendicular offsets to the objects on either side of the line can be taken
options.B: Measuring the length of the survey line directly in the field
options.C: Determining the reduced levels of the points along the survey line
options.D: Establishing the straight line between two survey stations by ranging

e: A cross staff is used to set out a right angle at a point on the survey line, so perpendicular offsets to objects on either side can be taken.

q: Where the execution of a railway project requires the diversion of forest land, the project authority is required to:

options.A: Occupy the land on payment of a nominal fee to the Forest Department
options.B: Plant trees within the railway land in lieu of the forest land, without any formal approval
options.C: Obtain prior approval for the diversion under the Forest (Conservation) Act, and bear the cost of compensatory afforestation and the net present value of the forest land diverted
options.D: Obtain the permission of the local panchayat for taking over the land

e: Diversion of forest land needs prior approval under the Forest (Conservation) Act, and the project authority bears compensatory afforestation cost and the net present value of the land diverted.

q: In levelling work for a proposed railway work, an 'intermediate sight' is:

options.A: The first staff reading taken from a setting of the instrument, on a point of known reduced level
options.B: A staff reading taken, from the same setting of the instrument, on a point between the back sight and the foresight, whose reduced level is required, the instrument not being shifted for taking it
options.C: The last staff reading taken from a setting of the instrument, on the point from which the levelling is carried forward
options.D: The staff reading taken on the bench mark for verifying the height of the instrument at the close of the day's work

e: An intermediate sight is a staff reading taken from the same instrument setting on a point between the back sight and the foresight, without shifting the instrument.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Land for a 'special railway project' can be acquired under the special provisions contained in the Railways Act, 1989, which provide for the acquisition of land for such projects through the competent authority.
2. The acquisition proceedings for such a project are carried out by the Rail Land Development Authority on behalf of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: the Railways Act, 1989 contains special provisions for acquiring land for a special railway project through the competent authority. Statement 2 is wrong: acquisition is not carried out by the Rail Land Development Authority.

q: The weight of one metre length of a steel reinforcement bar is given by the formula d2/162 kilograms, where d is the diameter of the bar in millimetres. The weight of one metre length of a bar of 20 millimetres diameter is:

options.A: 0.89 kilogram
options.B: 1.58 kilograms
options.C: 3.86 kilograms
options.D: 2.47 kilograms

e: Weight per metre = d2 / 162 = 20 x 20 / 162 = 400 / 162 = 2.47 kilograms for a 20 mm bar.

q: During the execution of a work, earth and other materials are obtained from the excavation made for the work and from the dismantling of existing structures at the site. As regards such materials, the correct position is that:

options.A: They become the property of the contractor, who may sell them and retain the proceeds
options.B: They may be removed by the contractor from the site without any reference to the Engineer
options.C: They are the property of the Railways, and are used on the work or disposed of as directed by the Engineer, the contractor having no right to remove or sell them on his own
options.D: Their value is adjusted against the earnest money of the contractor at the close of the work

e: Materials from excavation or dismantling at site are Railway property; they are used or disposed of as the Engineer directs and the contractor cannot remove or sell them on his own.

q: In chain surveying for a proposed railway work, the 'base line' is:

options.A: The line joining two points whose reduced levels are known, used as the datum for the levelling
options.B: The short line joining a survey station to an object whose position is to be located
options.C: The line run along the boundary of the land proposed to be acquired for the work
options.D: The main and ordinarily the longest line of the survey framework, run through the centre of the area, from which the other survey lines and the offsets to the details are taken

e: The base line is the main, ordinarily longest, line of the survey framework run through the centre of the area, from which other survey lines and offsets to details are taken.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Volume I of the Indian Railway Financial Code broadly contains the general rules relating to control over expenditure, sanctions, estimates, tenders and contracts.
2. Volume II of the Indian Railway Financial Code contains the Accounts Code, dealing with the classification of transactions and the maintenance of accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Financial Code Volume I lays down the general rules on control over expenditure, sanctions, estimates, tenders and contracts, while Volume II carries the classification appendices (Appendices I-III) prescribing the heads under which transactions are classified and accounts maintained - both statements are correct (Answer: C).

q: A bank undertakes to pay the Railways in case a contractor defaults in performing his obligations under a contract. This arrangement, involving three parties - the creditor, the principal debtor and the surety - is a contract of:

options.A: Indemnity
options.B: Guarantee
options.C: Agency
options.D: Bailment

e: A bank undertaking to pay on the contractor's default is a contract of guarantee under the Contract Act, with three parties: creditor (Railways), principal debtor (contractor) and surety (bank).

q: In the law of contracts, the publication of a Notice Inviting Tender by the Railways amounts to:

options.A: An invitation to offer, the tender submitted by a tenderer being the offer
options.B: An offer, which the tenderer accepts by submitting his tender
options.C: An acceptance of the terms of the tenderers
options.D: A concluded agreement with all the tenderers

e: A Notice Inviting Tender is only an invitation to offer; the tender submitted in response is the offer, which the Railways may accept or reject.

q: A contractor has executed work under a contract which is subsequently found to be unenforceable. He can still recover reasonable payment for the work actually done by him under the principle known as:

options.A: Liquidated damages
options.B: Specific performance
options.C: Injunction
options.D: Quantum meruit

e: For work actually done under a contract later found unenforceable, reasonable payment is recoverable on quantum meruit, i.e. payment for the value of work done.

q: A tenderer offers an Insurance Surety Bond issued by an insurance company, instead of a bank guarantee, towards the performance security for a work. Under the instructions issued under the General Financial Rules, such a bond:

options.A: Cannot be accepted in any Government procurement
options.B: Is accepted as a valid form of security, in lieu of a bank guarantee, towards earnest money and performance security
options.C: Is acceptable only in contracts for insurance services
options.D: Is treated as a personal guarantee of the insurance agent

e: Under GFR instructions, an Insurance Surety Bond issued by an insurance company is an accepted form of security in lieu of a bank guarantee for earnest money and performance security.

q: A 'reverse auction' in e-procurement is a process in which, after the initial price bids have been opened:

options.A: The bidders successively lower their quoted prices online during the auction period, and the lowest bid at the close of the auction is considered for award
options.B: The contract is awarded to the bidder who had quoted the highest price in the initial bids
options.C: The bidders are permitted to withdraw their earnest money before the auction closes
options.D: The tender is cancelled and invited afresh with revised conditions

e: In a reverse auction, after initial price bids are opened, bidders successively lower their prices online during the auction and the lowest bid at close is considered for award.

q: The main object of inviting an Expression of Interest at the initial stage of a complex or public-private partnership project is to:

options.A: Award the work without any further tendering
options.B: Fix the earnest money to be deposited by the bidders
options.C: Gauge the interest of the market and shortlist capable parties for the subsequent detailed bidding stage
options.D: Obtain the sanction of the Railway Board for the project

e: An Expression of Interest is invited to gauge market interest and shortlist capable parties for the subsequent detailed bidding stage of a complex or PPP project.

q: A concessionaire reports that financial closure has been achieved for his public-private partnership project. This means that:

options.A: The project has been completed and opened to traffic
options.B: The concession agreement has been registered with the Registrar of Companies
options.C: The first annuity payment has been released to the concessionaire
options.D: The concessionaire has tied up the required debt and equity for the project and the conditions for drawal of the funds are in place

e: Financial closure means the concessionaire has tied up the required debt and equity for the PPP project and the conditions for drawing the funds are in place.

q: CPM and PERT, used in connection with major railway projects, are techniques for:

options.A: Fixing the rates of items in the schedule of rates
options.B: Planning, scheduling and monitoring the progress of major projects
options.C: Preparing the Pink Book of the Railway
options.D: Calculating the liquidated damages payable by a contractor

e: CPM and PERT are network techniques used for planning, scheduling and monitoring the progress of major projects.

q: An 'out-turn' estimate furnished by a Railway during the course of a financial year is an estimate of the:

options.A: Likely actual expenditure for the year, assessed from the progress of expenditure up to the time of its preparation
options.B: Budget estimates for the next financial year
options.C: Appropriation voted by Parliament for the year
options.D: Throw-forward liability of works in progress

e: An out-turn estimate gives the likely actual expenditure for the year, assessed from the progress of expenditure up to the time it is prepared.

q: Deposits such as earnest money and security deposit, which remain unclaimed for more than three years after they have become refundable, are:

options.A: Refunded to the contractors along with interest
options.B: Transferred to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Credited to the revenues of the Railways as lapsed deposits
options.D: Held in deposit indefinitely until claimed

e: Earnest money and security deposits unclaimed for more than three years after becoming refundable are credited to Railway revenues as lapsed deposits.

q: A work on railway land is to be executed with funds provided under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS). Such a work is executed by the Railways:

options.A: As an ordinary railway work chargeable to Capital
options.B: Only through State Government agencies
options.C: Only after the work is included in the Pink Book with the Board's sanction
options.D: As a deposit work, against the funds deposited for the purpose

e: An MPLADS-funded work on railway land is executed by the Railways as a deposit work against the funds deposited for the purpose.

q: Under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971, the authority before whom eviction proceedings in respect of unauthorised occupation of railway land are conducted is the:

options.A: Station Master of the nearest station
options.B: Estate Officer appointed under the Act
options.C: Divisional Commercial Manager
options.D: Land Licensing Officer of the division

e: Eviction proceedings for unauthorised occupation of railway land under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971 are conducted before the Estate Officer appointed under the Act.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a Class-I local supplier is a supplier whose goods, services or works have local content of 50 per cent or more.
2. A Class-II local supplier is a supplier whose goods, services or works have local content of 20 per cent or more but less than 50 per cent.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: under the Make in India Order, a Class-I local supplier has local content of 50 per cent or more, and a Class-II supplier has 20 per cent or more but less than 50 per cent.

q: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, the minimum share of the total annual procurement which every Central Ministry, Department and public sector undertaking is required to make from micro and small enterprises is:

options.A: 10 per cent
options.B: 15 per cent
options.C: 20 per cent
options.D: 25 per cent

e: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, the minimum annual procurement share from MSEs for Central Ministries, Departments and PSUs is 25 per cent.

q: Major projects such as new lines, gauge conversion and doubling, executed by the construction organisation of a zonal railway, are carried out under the overall control of the:

options.A: Divisional Railway Manager
options.B: Principal Chief Engineer
options.C: Chief Administrative Officer (Construction)
options.D: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer

e: Major construction projects like new lines, gauge conversion and doubling are executed by the construction organisation under the overall control of the Chief Administrative Officer (Construction).

q: The 'fineness modulus' of an aggregate used in concrete work is:

options.A: The percentage of the aggregate passing through the finest sieve
options.B: An index number representing the fineness or coarseness of the aggregate, obtained from its sieve analysis
options.C: The ratio of the weight of the aggregate to its volume
options.D: The crushing strength of the aggregate

e: Fineness modulus is an index number from sieve analysis representing the fineness or coarseness of an aggregate used in concrete.

q: The 'shear strength' of a soil at the site of a foundation is its:

options.A: Resistance to failure by sliding along a plane within the soil mass
options.B: Capacity to allow water to pass through it
options.C: Ability to consolidate under a sustained load
options.D: Resistance to being penetrated by a standard cone

e: Shear strength of soil is its resistance to failure by sliding along a plane within the soil mass at the foundation site.

q: 'Curing' of concrete placed in a work consists of:

options.A: Removing the shuttering immediately after the concrete has set
options.B: Applying a coat of paint over the surface of the concrete
options.C: Heating the concrete to accelerate its setting
options.D: Keeping the concrete moist for the prescribed period so that it attains its designed strength properly

e: Curing means keeping placed concrete moist for the prescribed period so it gains its designed strength properly.

q: The lateral ties, known as stirrups, provided in a reinforced cement concrete beam are necessary mainly for:

options.A: Increasing the compressive strength of the concrete
options.B: Reducing the deflection of the beam
options.C: Resisting the shear forces in the beam and holding the main reinforcement in position
options.D: Protecting the main reinforcement against corrosion

e: Stirrups, the lateral ties in an RCC beam, mainly resist shear forces in the beam and hold the main reinforcement in position.

q: A bag of ordinary Portland cement is marked '53 grade'. The figure 53 indicates the:

options.A: Fineness to which the cement is ground
options.B: Minimum compressive strength, in newtons per square millimetre, which the cement attains at 28 days
options.C: Setting time of the cement in minutes
options.D: Proportion of clinker present in the cement

e: In 53 grade OPC, 53 indicates the minimum compressive strength in newtons per square millimetre attained by the cement at 28 days.

q: The rising of moisture from the ground into the walls of a building above the plinth is prevented by providing, at about plinth level, a:

options.A: Damp proof course
options.B: String course
options.C: Cornice
options.D: Weathering course

e: A damp proof course provided at about plinth level prevents moisture rising from the ground into the walls above the plinth.

q: Water which accumulates behind a retaining wall is drained out, and the pressure on the wall thereby relieved, through:

options.A: Expansion joints
options.B: Construction joints
options.C: Ventilation openings
options.D: Weep holes

e: Weep holes drain out water accumulated behind a retaining wall, relieving the water pressure on the wall.

q: For the protection of bridge foundations and embankments, wire crates filled with stones or boulders are used. Such crates are known as:

options.A: Cofferdams
options.B: Caissons
options.C: Gabions
options.D: Groynes

e: Wire crates filled with stones or boulders used to protect bridge foundations and embankments are called gabions.

q: A hollow structure which is sunk into the ground or the river bed and forms a part of the permanent foundation of a bridge is known as a:

options.A: Cofferdam
options.B: Caisson
options.C: Grillage
options.D: Raft

e: A caisson is a hollow structure sunk into the ground or river bed which forms part of the permanent foundation of a bridge.

q: In a turnout, the 'flangeway' is the:

options.A: Clear gap provided between the running rail and the check or guard rail, through which the flange of the wheel passes
options.B: Distance between the two running rails of the track
options.C: Raised portion of the outer rail on a curve
options.D: Gap left between the ends of two adjoining rails at a joint

e: The flangeway in a turnout is the clear gap between the running rail and the check or guard rail through which the wheel flange passes.

q: 'Grade compensation' provided on a curved portion of a railway section means the:

options.A: Raising of the outer rail above the inner rail on the curve
options.B: Provision of a transition curve between the straight and the curve
options.C: Widening of the gauge on the curve
options.D: Easing, that is flattening, of the gradient on the curve to offset the additional resistance offered by the curve to the movement of trains

e: Grade compensation means easing or flattening the gradient on a curve to offset the extra resistance the curve offers to train movement.

q: The 'newel post' in a staircase of a building is the:

options.A: Horizontal part of a step on which the foot is placed
options.B: Vertical face of a step between two treads
options.C: Stout post provided at the top or bottom of a flight of steps, which supports the handrail
options.D: Flat platform provided between two flights of steps

e: The newel post is the stout post at the top or bottom of a flight of steps which supports the handrail of the staircase.

q: A road over-bridge is constructed in lieu of a level crossing at a total cost of Rs 18,00,000 on a cost-sharing basis, the cost being shared equally between the Railways and the State Government. The share borne by the State Government is:
e: State Government share = 50 per cent of Rs 18,00,000 = Rs 9,00,000, the cost being shared equally with the Railways.

q: A contractor who has not furnished his Permanent Account Number (PAN) is paid Rs 6,00,000 for a works contract. The tax deductible at source under Section 206AA of the Income-tax Act, at the rate of 20 per cent, amounts to:
e: TDS under Section 206AA for a payee without PAN = 20 per cent of Rs 6,00,000 = Rs 1,20,000.
